newsitem.title: USA: Genzyme, Diacrin therapies gain FDA designations.
newsitem.headline: Genzyme, Diacrin therapies gain FDA designations.

text.p: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has granted orphan drug designation to therapies for Parkinson's disease and Huntington's disease made by a 50-50 joint venture between Genzyme Corp's Tissue Repair Division and Diacrin Inc, the companies said on Wednesday.
The therapies are NeuroCell-PD for advanced Parkinson's disease and NeuroCell-HD for Huntington's disease.
The designations -- two for each therapy -- are the first step in gaining seven-year exclusivity from the FDA for marketing the therapies, Diacrin Chief Executive Thomas Fraser said.

The exclusivity would go to the first developer of the therapies to receive FDA approval following clinical trials, he said. He said pending positive clinical trials and FDA approval, the companies could start marketing the therapies as soon as late 1999.

The companies announced their joint venture in September. Genzyme has committed $40 million toward the venture and Diacrin $10 million, according to Fraser. Diacrin had worked independently on the therapies for "a few years" before entering the venture, Fraser added.
Both therapies involve transplanted porcine neural cells, the companies said.
The companies said that between 115,000 and 155,000 people have advanced Parkinson's disease in the United States and about 25,000 people have Huntington's disease.
Fraser said it was too early to estimate how much revenue the therapies could generate if the FDA approved them.
